observation_summary: The StringUtils methods fail to correctly handle Unicode supplementary characters (which are represented as surrogate pairs in Java). The methods iterate over characters individually, causing them to incorrectly match or mismatch when a high surrogate is encountered, as they do not verify the presence of the corresponding low surrogate.
hypothesis: The StringUtils methods (containsAny, containsNone, indexOfAny, etc.) fail to correctly handle Unicode supplementary characters because they treat strings as sequences of 16-bit char values without accounting for surrogate pairs. When a high surrogate is encountered, the methods do not verify if it is part of a valid supplementary character pair, leading to incorrect matches or mismatches when the search criteria involve these characters.
prediction: I expected to see that the implementation of these methods iterates through the string character by character and performs comparisons on individual chars, failing to check for the presence of a low surrogate following a high surrogate when a match is found.
experiment_rationale: The failure is clearly related to how the methods process characters. The bug report and test cases confirm that supplementary characters (surrogate pairs) are not handled correctly. The ODC type is Algorithm/Method because the logic for searching/matching characters is fundamentally flawed for the specific data type (Unicode supplementary characters).
reasoning_summary: The bug is a classic case of failing to account for surrogate pairs in Java strings. The methods perform character-by-character iteration, which is insufficient for Unicode supplementary characters. This is an algorithmic flaw in how the search/match procedure is implemented.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves adding checks, the core issue is the procedural logic of how the string is traversed and matched, which is an algorithmic concern.
